newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Opening of Israel international calls mart delayed.
newsitem.headline: Opening of Israel international calls mart delayed.

text.p: The opening of Israel's international calls market to competition was delayed on Tuesday as the Communications Ministry tried to settle a dispute over rates with Bezeq Israel Telecom, the ministry said.
"Competition will not begin today as planned. Competition will start in a few days," Communications Ministry spokeswoman Ayala Bar told Reuters.

Communications Minister Limor Livnat accused state-owned Bezeq of violating the law and exploiting its dominant market position after the company published proposed international tariffs, as much as 80 percent below current rates, without ministry approval.
Livnat said Bezeq International, Bezeq's international phone service subsidiary, was offering customers "dumping prices" and asked Israel's anti-trust authority to intervene.
Bezeq International spokeswoman Dafna Triwaks said anti-trust officials had searched its offices and "we are cooperating with them entirely."

Under the law, Bezeq is subject to strict supervision during the first six months of the new competitive market. Bezeq said the ministry knew of its ad campaign and that it had not violated the law because the new rates were not yet in force.

Bar said talks were ongoing between the ministry, Bezeq and the two new providers, Golden Lines, controlled by SBC Communications Inc, Italy's Stet and three Israeli partners, and Barak, controlled by Sprint Corp, France Telecom, Deutsche Telekom, Clal Israel and Matav Cable Systems Media Ltd.
She declined to comment on the content of the negotiations.
